options.label: `find_session` can return NULL and is dereferenced
options.whyWrong: Lines 3-4 already handle NULL; the problem is use of a freed pointer, not a null one.

options.label: When the session is expired it is freed on line 7, but lines 11-12 still dereference `sess`, reading and writing memory that has been returned to the allocator
`snprintf` may truncate a long username
options.whyWrong: Truncation is benign; it is not the memory-safety defect.

options.label: Set sess = NULL after free_session(sess)
options.whyWrong: Lines 11-12 would then dereference NULL and crash; the code still uses an invalid pointer instead of avoiding the use.

options.label: After freeing an expired session, return immediately instead of continuing to use it
Replace free_session(sess) with free(sess)
options.whyWrong: This still frees the object and leaves the later dereferences dangling (and skips unlinking it from the table).

training.exploit: Request an expired session so line 7 frees `sess`. The allocator may hand that chunk to another concurrent allocation before line 11 runs, so writing `sess->last_seen` corrupts the new object and reading `sess->user` dereferences attacker-influenced data. With heap grooming this turns into controlled memory corruption — crashes at minimum, code execution at worst.

hints.line: The object is touched after it was released.
hints.why: What state is `sess` in on line 11 when the session was expired?
hints.fix: Stop using the object once it's been freed.

writeup.summary: On the expired branch, `free_session(sess)` releases the object and unlinks it, but control falls through to lines 11-12, which write and read `sess` — a use-after-free. Between the free and the use, the allocator can reissue that memory to another allocation, so the write corrupts an unrelated object and the read returns attacker-influenceable bytes; careful heap grooming escalates this to code execution. The fix returns immediately after freeing (or only refreshes sessions that weren't freed), so the freed pointer is never dereferenced.
